mtp_verdict: NOT BLOCKED. The MTP/draft head survives the NVFP4 repack in the overwhelming majority of candidates, and it survives in BF16 (unquantized), which is strictly better for the drafter than the FP8 MTP we serve today. Verified by fetching model.safetensors.index.json and, where needed, reading the raw safetensors headers over HTTP range requests. All 15 expected tensors present with exactly the local 3.6 shapes in: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (dedicated model_mtp.safetensors, 0.85 GB), RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (shard 3; tensor-audit.json asserts mtp_tensor_count 15), sakamakismile/Qwen3.8-27B-MTP-NVFP4 (dedicated model-mtp-bf16.safetensors), gittensor-model-hub/...-RTX5090, Inferact, Mantrah, vroomfondel, dbirks, dbrasdasilva, Peutlefaire, nm-testing, huginnfork, and ~20 more in the sweep. Every one of them lists the MTP modules in the quantizer ignore/exclude set (either enumerated module-by-module, or as the regex 're:^mtp.*' / glob 'mtp*'), so the head is deliberately preserved rather than accidentally surviving. Confirmed tensor shapes: mtp.fc.weight [5120,10240], mtp.norm/.pre_fc_norm_embedding/.pre_fc_norm_hidden [5120], mtp.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj [12288,5120], k_proj/v_proj [1024,5120], o_proj [5120,6144], q_norm/k_norm [256], mlp.gate/up_proj [17408,5120], mlp.down_proj [5120,17408], input_layernorm/post_attention_layernorm [5120]. nvfp4_details:
FORMAT SPLIT. Two incompatible on-disk conventions are in circulation, both nominally 'NVFP4', and vLLM dispatches them through different code paths. (A) compressed-tensors / llm-compressor: quantization_config.quant_method='compressed-tensors', format='nvfp4-pack-quantized' (or 'mixed-precision' when combined with FP8 groups), config_groups with targets/ignore, and tensor names weight_packed (U8, shape [out, in/2]), weight_scale (F8_E4M3, shape [out, in/16]), weight_global_scale (F32 scalar), input_global_scale (F32 scalar). Used by unsloth, nm-testing, sakamakismile, Peutlefaire, dbirks, huginnfork, cloudnathan5. (B) NVIDIA ModelOpt: a separate hf_quant_config.json with producer.name='modelopt', quantization.quant_algo NVFP4 or MIXED_PRECISION, kv_cache_quant_algo, group_size 16, and either quantized_layers{} or exclude_modules[]; tensor names weight (U8 [out, in/2]), weight_scale (F8_E4M3 [out, in/16]), weight_scale_2 (F32 scalar global), input_scale (F32 scalar). Used by RadixArk, gittensor, Inferact, Mantrah, vroomfondel, dbrasdasilva, r0b0tlab. SCALE FORMAT is consistent across both: block/group size 16 along the input dim, per-block scale in float8_e4m3, plus one FP32 global (second-level) scale per tensor - i.e. the standard NVFP4 two-level E2M1 + E4M3 + FP32 scheme. Activations are W4A4 with dynamic 'local' per-group input quant in most repos; huginnfork is the lone A16 weight-only variant.
WHAT IS EXCLUDED, per candidate. Universal exclusions across every serious repo: the entire vision tower (333 tensors, ~1.1 GB BF16, model.visual.*), model.language_model.embed_tokens, linear_attn.conv1d (the GDN depthwise conv), linear_attn.norm, all RMSNorms, A_log, dt_bias, and the whole mtp.* subtree. lm_head: BF16 in sakamakismile/Peutlefaire/gittensor/Inferact/dbrasdasilva; FP8 per-channel in unsloth/nm-testing and (as a separate FP8 group) Mantrah; NVFP4 W4A4 in RadixArk and r0b0tlab. GDN convs are never quantized anywhere - good, that protects the recurrent state. GDN in_proj_a/in_proj_b ([48,5120] decay and dt projections): left BF16 by unsloth, gittensor, vroomfondel, Inferact, dbirks (matching Qwen's own official FP8 exclusion list); quantized to 4-bit by sakamakismile, Peutlefaire, dbrasdasilva, Mantrah - treat that as a quality landmine for a GDN-hybrid, because Qwen deliberately excluded exactly those two modules in both the 3.6 and 3.8 official FP8 recipes. GDN in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z/out_proj: FP8 in unsloth and RadixArk, NVFP4 in gittensor/Mantrah/sakamakismile, BF16 (unquantized) in Inferact. Full-attention self_attn q/k/v/o: FP8 in unsloth and RadixArk, NVFP4 in sakamakismile/gittensor/Inferact/Mantrah/dbrasdasilva.
KV CACHE. unsloth/nm-testing carry calibrated FP8 kv scales as per-layer self_attn.k_scale/v_scale BF16 scalars (kv_cache_scheme num_bits 8, tensor strategy, static_minmax observer). RadixArk, gittensor and vroomfondel declare kv_cache_quant_algo FP8 but RadixArk's own qualification.json admits the scales were NOT calibrated ('no scaling factors provided, defaulting to 1.0'). sakamakismile, Peutlefaire, dbirks, Mantrah, huginnfork declare no kv quantization at all.
UNSLOTH RECIPE IN DETAIL (the one I recommend). Two config groups. group_0 = FP8, weights per-channel static (weight_scale BF16 [out,1]), activations per-token dynamic, targeting regex 're:.*self_attn\\.(q|k|v|o)_proj$', 're:.*linear_attn\\.(in_proj_qkv|in_proj_z|out_proj)$', 're:.*lm_head', and 're:.*layers\\.(56|57|58|59|60|61|62|63)\\.mlp\\.(gate|up|down)_proj$' - i.e. the last 8 transformer layers' MLPs are deliberately held at FP8 rather than FP4. group_1 = nvfp4-pack-quantized W4A4 g16 on every other 're:.*mlp\\.(gate|up|down)_proj$'. 303-entry ignore covering visual.*, linear_attn.in_proj_a/in_proj_b/norm, and 're:^mtp.*'. Verified from the raw header: layer 0 in_proj_qkv is F8_E4M3 [10240,5120] + weight_scale BF16 [10240,1]; layer 0 mlp.gate_proj is U8 weight_packed [17408,2560] + F8_E4M3 weight_scale [17408,320] + F32 globals; layer 60 mlp.gate_proj is F8_E4M3 [17408,5120] (confirming the last-8-layers FP8 carve-out); lm_head F8_E4M3 [248320,5120]; embed_tokens BF16 [248320,5120].
recommendation:
DOWNLOAD ORDER. (1) FIRST, and before touching NVFP4 at all: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, 30.89 GB. This is not a detour - it is the cheapest possible de-risking of the whole port, because it is structurally identical to the checkpoint we serve today (same 66-file layers-N/mtp/outside layout, same 1606 tensors, same 882-entry FP8 exclusion list, same 30.87 GB payload as Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8) AND the 3.8 architecture is byte-identical to 3.6. It should slot into the existing patched-vLLM pipeline with zero code changes, which cleanly separates 'did the model change break us' from 'did NVFP4 break us'. It also gives you the honest FP8 3.8 baseline you need to attribute any B1/B4 delta and any SWE-bench QC delta to quantization rather than to the model refresh. (2) PRIMARY NVFP4: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 23.44 GB. Reasons: compressed-tensors is the most battle-tested NVFP4 path in vLLM; the recipe is the most conservative of the field (GDN in_proj_a/in_proj_b left BF16 exactly as Qwen's own FP8 recipe does, attention and GDN projections at FP8 rather than FP4, last 8 MLP layers held at FP8, embed BF16, calibrated FP8 KV scales); MTP is fully intact in BF16 in its own model_mtp.safetensors; the file set is complete (tokenizer.json, vocab.json, merges.txt, chat_template.jinja, both preprocessor configs); apache-2.0, ungated, 276k downloads, and it is the productized mirror of the Neural Magic reference quant (nm-testing/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-FP8, byte-identical config_groups and tensor count). Expected weight-stream reduction vs the FP8 we serve: 30.87 -> 22.57+0.85 GB of safetensors, about 24%, which on a 273 GB/s bandwidth-bound GB10 is roughly the size of the decode win available. (3) FALLBACK: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, 21.95 GB. Take this if unsloth's compressed-tensors mixed-precision path won't load on the pinned image, or if you want the more aggressive weight-stream cut. It is the only checkpoint in the entire field with published verification: tensor-audit.json (verdict pass), GSM8K 97.27% with zero truncations/errors, and - critically for us - a measured MTP speculative-decoding acceptance length of 2.775 on Blackwell hardware. It uses the ModelOpt hf_quant_config path instead. Its one real liability is an NVFP4-quantized lm_head, which is both a logits-quality risk for the K64 drafter vocab and a plausible vLLM loader incompatibility. (4) SECOND FALLBACK if you need the last GB and accept community risk: gittensor-model-hub/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-RTX5090 (20.62 GB, ModelOpt, BF16 lm_head, GDN in_proj_a/b protected) - same exclusion philosophy as unsloth but 4-bit on the GDN projections. (5) Only if you decide to re-quantize in-house: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B BF16, 55.59 GB - and note that a local ModelOpt/llm-compressor run would let you drop the ~1.1 GB vision tower and pick your own lm_head precision, which no public repo except dbrasdasilva does.
TOTAL DOWNLOAD: 54.33 GB for the recommended two-step (FP8 baseline 30.89 + unsloth NVFP4 23.44). 76.28 GB if you also pull RadixArk as the fallback. 23.44 GB if you skip the FP8 baseline and go straight at NVFP4 (not advised).
RED FLAGS, ranked. (a) NO OFFICIAL NVFP4 EXISTS. I confirmed by direct API probe that Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-FP4, RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 and RedHatAI/Qwen3.8-27B-FP4 all return 401 (do not exist), that the nvidia org publishes nothing named Qwen3.8, and that RedHatAI publishes only Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and its FP8 - not the 27B. The full Qwen org listing for this family is exactly four repos: Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8. Every NVFP4 option is therefore a community repack. (b) EVERYTHING IS TWO DAYS OLD. Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B lastModified 2026-08-14; the community NVFP4 repos are dated 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-16. Essentially none of them has been shaken out by real usage, and several were pushed in the last 24 hours. Expect churn - re-check the field in a week. (c) PRIOR ART SAYS NVFP4 HAS ALREADY BITTEN THIS PROJECT ON THIS HARDWARE. origin/main:docs/LLD-01-vLLM-Serving-Layer-v0.4.md lines 149-156 and 669-670 record 'ARM64 NVFP4 CUDA crash - HIGH for NVFP4' and 'Qwen3.5 NVFP4 accuracy degradation - HIGH', and docs/codex-bench-spec-v2_3.md:164-166 records an open vLLM bug for Qwen3.5 NVFP4 crashing on ARM64 GB10 with CUDA illegal instructions plus a separate poor-accuracy report. NVFP4 was consequently confined to a 'Sprint 0.5 appendix only'. That risk was never retired in-repo. Whether it still reproduces on the pinned cu130-nightly 0.19.2rc1.dev134 image is the single highest-value thing to test first, and it is testable with a small smoke run before committing to the full campaign. (d) FR13's own doctrine currently forbids this. origin/main:FR13_KERNEL_SPEEDUP_HYPOTHESES.md:81 states model-wide NVFP4 is 'LOSSY (~1% degradation), breaks the bit-exact lossless gate' and brushes the banned weight-re-streaming rule, marked 'Do not propose'. Porting to NVFP4 is a deliberate scope change away from bit-exact losslessness toward quality-bounded parity; the QC suite becomes the gate, not bit-exactness. Make that explicit in the campaign kickoff so it does not get relitigated mid-run. (e) The MTP loader must tolerate an unquantized BF16 head inside a quantized checkpoint (see mtp_verdict). (f) Three repos silently drop the MTP head entirely - lokeshe09, YCWTG, mlx-community - and r0b0tlab uploaded only the MTP shard and none of the model; do not let an automated 'pick the smallest NVFP4' heuristic near this list. (g) Incomplete file sets: nm-testing and dbirks are missing vocab.json/merges.txt/preprocessor configs; vroomfondel is missing merges.txt; dbrasdasilva has no index.json or preprocessor configs. (h) Every candidate except dbrasdasilva ships the full 333-tensor BF16 vision tower (~1.1 GB) that this text-only campaign will never touch. (i) Licensing is clean throughout - apache-2.0, ungated, no gate acceptance needed on any recommended repo (nm-testing declares no license, another reason to prefer unsloth's mirror). (j) An orthogonal opportunity worth flagging to the orchestrator: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark is a purpose-trained 1.36B BF16 speculator for this exact model with published acceptance length 3.39 mean over 1164 requests (HumanEval 3.47, MBPP 3.67, LiveCodeBench 2.94) versus the built-in MTP head's ~2.775. It is SGLang-only today and does not fit the FR13 vLLM MTP path, but it is direct evidence that the MTP head is not the acceptance ceiling for Qwen3.8-27B.
arch_36_summary: Qwen3.6-27B (local /home/mark/shared/models/qwen3.6-27b-fp8, and the official Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B I fetched for cross-check): architectures ['Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration'], model_type qwen3_5, a NATIVE vision-language model (text_config + vision_config, image_token_id 248056, video_token_id 248057, vision_start/end 248053/248054, language_model_only false). Text tower: 64 layers, layer_types is an explicit 64-entry list driven by full_attention_interval 4 giving full_attention at indices 3,7,11,...,63 (16 full-attention layers) and linear_attention at all other indices (48 GDN layers); hidden_size 5120, intermediate_size 17408, num_attention_heads 24, num_key_value_heads 4, head_dim 256, attn_output_gate true (so q_proj is [12288,5120] = 24*256*2 for value+gate), attention_bias false, hidden_act silu, rms_norm_eps 1e-06. GDN: linear_num_key_heads 16, linear_num_value_heads 48, linear_key_head_dim 128, linear_value_head_dim 128, linear_conv_kernel_dim 4, output_gate_type swish, mamba_ssm_dtype float32. vocab_size 248320, tie_word_embeddings false (separate lm_head [248320,5120]). MTP: mtp_num_hidden_layers 1, mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings false; realised as 15 tensors - mtp.fc [5120,10240], mtp.norm, mtp.pre_fc_norm_embedding, mtp.pre_fc_norm_hidden, and one FULL-attention block mtp.layers.0 (self_attn q[12288,5120]/k[1024,5120]/v[1024,5120]/o[5120,6144] + q_norm/k_norm [256] + SwiGLU mlp gate/up [17408,5120], down [5120,17408] + input/post_attention layernorms). RoPE: rope_type default, rope_theta 1e7, partial_rotary_factor 0.25, mrope_interleaved true, mrope_section [11,11,10], max_position_embeddings 262144. Vision tower: depth 27, hidden 1152, intermediate 4304, 16 heads, patch 16, spatial_merge 2, temporal_patch 2, out_hidden 5120, num_position_embeddings 2304, deepstack_visual_indexes []. Local dir note: it is Qwen's official Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (README confirms) in the 66-file layers-N.safetensors + mtp.safetensors + outside.safetensors layout, 1606 tensors, ~29 GiB on disk. Its config.json has been locally patched (a config.json.lumo_pre_fp8_fix.bak backup exists with no quantization_config at all) to add quant_method fp8 / activation_scheme dynamic / weight_block_size [128,128] / a 371-entry modules_to_not_convert covering lm_head, embed_tokens, and every linear_attn conv1d/in_proj_a/in_proj_b. The local mtp.safetensors is FP8_E4M3 with 7 weight_scale_inv companions.
arch_38_summary: Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, revision e13a4f0e35203116364e3b3f3f0c82f6ef1afd3c, lastModified 2026-08-14, apache-2.0, ungated, 55.59 GB BF16 in 18 shards / 1199 tensors of which 333 are vision): architecturally IDENTICAL to Qwen3.6-27B on every field enumerated above - same Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration class, same qwen3_5/qwen3_5_text model types, same 64 layers with the same 48-GDN/16-full-attention layer_types list and full_attention_interval 4, same hidden 5120 / intermediate 17408 / 24 heads / 4 kv heads / head_dim 256 / attn_output_gate true, same GDN head geometry (16 key heads, 48 value heads, 128/128 dims, conv kernel 4, swish output gate), same vocab 248320, same tie_word_embeddings false, same mtp_num_hidden_layers 1 with the same 15-tensor MTP block and identical shapes, same RoPE (theta 1e7, partial_rotary_factor 0.25, mrope_interleaved, mrope_section [11,11,10], 262144 ctx), same vision tower geometry, same special token IDs, and a byte-identical generation_config.json. The ONLY delta in the entire config is transformers_version 4.57.1 -> 5.8.0.dev0 (plus the cosmetic removal of the redundant top-level torch_dtype key, whose value survives as text_config.dtype). The unsloth model card describes it as 'built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5' - the config confirms that literally. Qwen's own FP8 release (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, 30.89 GB, 66 files, 1606 tensors) likewise uses an unchanged recipe versus Qwen3.6-27B-FP8: same fp8/e4m3/dynamic/[128,128] block config and the same 882-entry modules_to_not_convert. Practical upshot for the port: nothing in the model definition, the tree-decode patcher, the GDN state handling, the K64 drafter vocab, or the MTP wiring needs to change for 3.8. The entire risk surface of this campaign is the NVFP4 quantization, not the model generation.
unknowns: Whether the pinned vLLM image (vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:3dbe092e..., cu130-nightly = 0.19.2rc1.dev134+gfe9c3d6c5, per origin/main:FR13_VLLM_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md) has CUTLASS NVFP4 GEMM kernels compiled for GB10's sm_121a at all. NVFP4 CUTLASS kernels are typically gated to sm_100a/sm_120a arch lists; sm_121 may fall outside. I did not open the image (no docker allowed in this recon) so this is unverified. This is the single biggest go/no-go unknown and it dominates the checkpoint choice.

Whether the historical 'ARM64 NVFP4 CUDA illegal instruction' crash recorded for Qwen3.5 NVFP4 in origin/main:docs/codex-bench-spec-v2_3.md:164-166 and docs/LLD-01-vLLM-Serving-Layer-v0.4.md:669 still reproduces on the current pinned image. The referenced upstream vLLM bug number is not recorded in the repo and I did not chase it.

Whether vLLM 0.19.2 supports BOTH NVFP4 conventions equally well - compressed-tensors 'nvfp4-pack-quantized' AND 'mixed-precision' (unsloth/RadixArk-alternative path) versus ModelOpt hf_quant_config 'MIXED_PRECISION' with per-module quantized_layers maps (RadixArk path). The mixed-precision variants in particular are newer and I could not confirm loader coverage without reading the image source.
Whether vLLM will accept an NVFP4-quantized lm_head (RadixArk, r0b0tlab). Many vLLM quant paths special-case lm_head as unquantized. Untested.

Whether the FR13 drafter/patcher loads mtp.* through a code path that assumes FP8 + weight_scale_inv. Every NVFP4 candidate ships BF16 MTP with no scale tensors. I did not read the drafter loader source - the repo at origin/main is almost entirely markdown and result artifacts, and I deliberately did not enter any worktree or run anything.

Actual quality of any NVFP4 repack beyond RadixArk's single GSM8K number (97.27%). No perplexity, no MMLU, no coding-benchmark, and above all no SWE-bench-Verified numbers exist for ANY of these checkpoints. The 16-task QC suite is the only thing that will tell you, and it must be run against the FP8 3.8 baseline for the comparison to mean anything.

How NVFP4 quantization of the TARGET affects MTP acceptance rate. RadixArk reports 2.775 acceptance length on their NVFP4 checkpoint but publishes no FP8 or BF16 control, so the degradation (if any) is unmeasured. Acceptance rate is a first-order term in the FR13 speedup, so a quantization-induced acceptance drop could eat the entire bandwidth win.

Whether any of these repacks silently altered the tokenizer or chat template. I compared file presence and the official generation_config.json (identical 3.6 vs 3.8) but did not diff tokenizer.json or chat_template.jinja bytes across community repos.

Weight fidelity itself. All of my inspection was HTTP metadata plus safetensors headers via range requests - I read tensor names, dtypes and shapes, never tensor DATA. A repo could have correct-looking headers over garbage payloads. Only RadixArk publishes checksums-of-evidence (evidence_sha256 block) and per-tensor audit; sakamakismile and r0b0tlab publish sha256 sidecars for some shards.

Which HF revision/commit each community repo will be at by download time. Several were modified today (2026-08-16: RadixArk, Mantrah, nm-testing). Pin an explicit revision SHA when you download or the artifact will not be reproducible.

Real on-device decode throughput. Every size figure here is a download/weight-stream proxy; I ran no GPU work per the read-only constraint. The 30.87 -> 23.42 GB (unsloth) or -> 21.92 GB (RadixArk) reduction is the theoretical bandwidth-bound ceiling, not a measurement.

Whether stripping the vision tower is worth doing. dbrasdasilva proves it is possible (language_model_only true, vision_config removed, 0 visual tensors) but I could not assess that repo's weight quality, and I do not know whether the FR13 patcher or the Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration vLLM implementation tolerates a config with no vision_config.
